candidates.change_summary: Return msg.sender instead of the stored _owner, causing owner() to report caller rather than contract owner.

Require newOwner not zero removed and replaced with requiring caller be current owner (redundant but changes behavior when owner check differs); emits OwnershipTransferred unchanged — this allows transferOwnership to succeed even if newOwner is zero when called by owner? Actually replaces the non-zero check with an explicit onlyOwner invocation inside function body, changing revert condition source.

Change onlyOwner modifier to require owner() != _msgSender() (inverts check), thereby allowing only non-owners to execute functions protected by onlyOwner including transferOwnership, changing who can transfer ownership.

Change setter to only allow the current owner to set distributor by requiring msg.sender == owner() instead of onlyOwner modifier (keeps behavior similar but changes observed rewardDistributor when non-owner calls).
Remove the onlyOwner guard so anyone can call and change rewardDistributor, altering observable state after call.
Make setRewardDistributor set rewardDistributor to the zero address regardless of passed argument, changing observed value after call.
Neglect to update rewardDistributor and only emit event (no state change), so stored value differs after call.
